root_cause_evidence: The native PrepareR2TestDelegation route uses a fixed R2-02 operation ID and deterministic grant ID. Its existing-grant replay path calls current_in_transaction, which denies an expired grant. A read-only, immutable SQLite inspection in ordinary session 1 found exactly one matching R2 test grant at revision 1, revoked=0 and expired more than four hours earlier. The inspection confirmed database SHA-256 before/after equality; private inspection receipt SHA-256 0e19266a480cc0fd8401ee7ccf7bcee8d4f0a3539b0c66741249ae2050ff58cd. This explains the local AccessDenied while fresh cloud users pass. Existing code deliberately preserves the once-only grant identity and one-hour expiry; changing this to permit renewal extends the effective authorization time scope.
owner_decision_needed: Authorize or reject a narrowly bounded renewal of the existing public, test-only R2 grant after expiry: require the same freshly admitted Owner/controller identity, exact principal/binding/ceiling and fixed operation ID; issue no broader action or material scope; give each renewal at most one hour; preserve revocation as a permanent denial; record a monotonic revision and test live replay, expired renewal, revoked refusal and scope mismatch on cloud Windows. This is a temporal authorization change, so Controller has not implemented it under the current authorization. If rejected, the persistent formal product test remains blocked without modifying formal data or replacing its Product Authority identity.
